New getPdfMediaBoxSizes(). * Most pdf files have an unencrypted MediaBox variable, which is used   by image renderers for scaling the raster output.  Some pdf files   have this set incorrectly.  If it is too big (e.g., by confusing   printer points with pixels, thus assuming the resolution is 72 ppi),   the renderer will make very large images.  This can be prevented   by finding the median mediabox sizes and modifying the resolution   in the renderer accordingly. * Modify prog/cleanpdf.c to avoid making large intermediate ppm files.

New getPdfPageSizes(). * This can be useful for determining resolution of page images; for   example, if the width is assumed to be 8.5 inches. * Knowing the size of the image allows more efficient modifications   where a program such as mutool is used to extract pages or images   for cleaning or better compression.  These images assume that the   media box is correct, and they accept a resolution as input.  The   media box is the size in printer points. We have seen scanned images   where the resolution was incorrectly assumed to be 72 ppi, resulting   in a large media box.  That large box, combined with an assumed   resolution of 300 ppi will cause large upscaling of about 4x in the   scanned image by the extractor.

Modify concatpdf.c to handle very large inputs and do better compression * For many image files (> 100), store them compressed with pixacomp. * By default, all images will be encoded as rgb using jpeg's DCT. * For efficient encoding of monochrome images, call with the one_bit   input parameter set to 1.  This will encode all images with tiffg4. * For mixed encoding, where images with color are encoded with DCT   and those without color are encoded with tiffg4, set both one_bit   and save_color input parameters to 1. * For determining color content, we are only using the colorfract   output from pixColorFract(), so make both outputs optional.

$TMPDIR path rewriting turned off on Unix A tesseract bug has surfaced, where $TMPDIR was set to /var/tmp, and someone writes a file to /tmp, and then tries to read it. genPathname() was rewriting the unix path "/tmp" --> TMPDIR, and the file was not found.  This is a bug.  Rewriting makes sense on Windows because there is no "/tmp", so it allows people to use "/tmp" as a shorthand for the actual Windows temp directory, which they don't even need to know. Phase 2 of reworking of the character recognition application * In particular, fixing the boot recognizer. * Made the unscaled set of labeled templates the primary data structure. * Recognizers are made from it for various actions, but until fully   trained, the goal is to store as many labeled unscaled templates   as are required. * All recognition now takes place by correlating the unknown with every   template, not with class average templates. * The only two remaining uses of average templates are for determining   outliers and doing greedy character splitting (recogCorrelationBestChar). * Padding deficient book-adapted recognizers (BAR) is done in a series   of steps, with the goal to extract more labeled unscaled templates   from the book. * In the event that not enough such templates can be found, a hybrid   BAR/BSR recognizer is easily made; it is used on scaled samples. * Bootstrap samples are scaled to a fixed height and augmented by   anisotropic horizontal scaling. * A mechanism is provided to optionally do image correlation with   skeletonized images that have been thickened so that the strokes   have constant width. * Several recog test programs have been added to demonstrate usage. * Operations where bootstrap recognizers (BSRs) are used to train   unlabeled samples from books are given in prog/recogtest2.c. * The steps to construct a BAR are shown in more detail in prog/recogtest3.c. * The default mechanism for separating touching characters remains   the greedy splitting in recogident.c.  Examples of its use are   in prog/recogtest1.c and prog/recogtest4.c. * And prog/recogtest5.c gives debug output for separating touching   characters with document image decoding (DID, recogdid.c). This uses   a HMM with character templates.

This also simplifies the generation and use of the boot recognizer, which makes a labeled pixa instead of a new recognizer. Some code has been commented out.
